text:
**Sometimes, but not always.** Bundles can save money when the manufacturer discounts the kit: for example, one price check found a BLUETTI AC180 bundle at **$649 versus $748 for the same components separately**, a $99 saving; an EcoFlow bundle was **$179 less** than its parts bought individually ([PowerSized price guide](https://powersized.com/solar-generator-kits/)).

But separate purchases can win if the power station is on sale or you choose a less expensive compatible panel. One comparison estimates an AC180 plus a third-party 200W panel at about **$659**, below a $729 bundle ([Dealectric comparison](https://dealectric.com/solar-generator-kit-vs-buying-separately)).

Compare the **actual sale prices** of the exact station and panel—not just list prices—and check that the panel’s voltage and connector work with the station. A bundle may still be worth it for the convenience of a matched setup and simpler support. ([Trek4Tech](https://www.trek4tech.com/articles/solar-generator-bundle-vs-buying-separately))

judge.top_pick: BLUETTI AC180 + 200 W Solar Panel Kit
products: BLUETTI AC180 + 200 W Solar Panel Kit
judge.why: The answer is mainly general advice and leads with the PowerSized $649 vs $748 AC180 example, with a secondary Dealectric comparison, so most figures don't come from dealectric.com.
